header.userPrompt:
Make `Agent.cheapOneShot` robust to cheap models that write a preamble before their answer.

Observed: the branch-naming one-shot (`BranchNamingStrategy.shortenPrompt`) ran haiku in the repo. A project CLAUDE.local.md told it to call an MCP tool first; the call was denied, and the reply was:

    Cannot call agents_md without permission; proceeding.

    implement-issue-196-followups

`Agent.payloadLine` (tools/src/main/scala/orca/agents/Agent.scala) took the first non-empty line, so the branch became `cannot-call-agents-md-without-permission-proceedin`.

Two changes:

1. `payloadLine`: when the reply has no fenced block, use the last non-empty line instead of the first. Keep the fenced-block preference. Check the other `cheapOneShot` callers (e.g. default commit messages) still get the right line, and update the scaladoc and tests.
2. Isolate `cheapOneShot` turns: no tools and no MCP servers (for claude, e.g. an empty `--tools` allowlist and `--strict-mcp-config` with no config). The one-shots only transform the prompt text; they need no repo access. Apply the same restriction on the other backends where their CLI supports it; where it does not, say so in the code.
